finding.title: Surface a user-visible error when EditTrackScreen._save() swallows a non-'permission-denied' TutorWriteException
finding.why: When the mocked/real trackEditService.editTrack() throws TutorWriteException with any code other than 'permission-denied' (e.g. 'internal', 'unavailable', 'deadline-exceeded' — all plausible on a tutor's flaky mobile connection, per the throw site in tutored_write_router.dart:355), the catch block's `if` is false, so it does nothing but `return`. The Save spinner clears (via the outer `finally`), the dialog is gone, and the user is left on the same screen with zero indication the edit failed — no snackbar, no navigation, no log call at this site. edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart is the only test file exercising EditTrackScreen's save flow, and its mockService.editTrack is stubbed with exactly one behavior file-wide (an unconditional `thenAnswer` success) — grepped for `thenThrow`/`TutorWriteException` and found none — so this silent-failure branch has never been exercised by any test.
finding.recommendation: Add an else/default branch to the catch that shows a generic error snackbar and logs via AppLogger for any code other than 'permission-denied'. Add a widget test that stubs mockService.editTrack to throw TutorWriteException('x', code: 'internal'), taps Save + Confirm, and asserts an error is surfaced to the user (must fail on current code).
acceptance_criteria: New widget test in edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart stubs mockService.editTrack to throw a TutorWriteException with a non-'permission-denied' code, taps Save Changes + confirms, and asserts a SnackBar/error message renders — red on current code, green after the fix
edit_track_screen.dart's catch block surfaces feedback (snackbar + AppLogger call) for every TutorWriteException code, not only 'permission-denied'
